source.title: How benign is benign overfitting?
source.authors: Amartya Sanyal; P. Dokania; Varun Kanade; P. Torr

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; some experimental values appear only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests label-noise overfitting and qualifies the notion of benign overfitting by showing effects on adversarial error while also reporting natural test error. Its robustness results do not test the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, size, or gap-measure claims.
record.gate_note: The paper's adversarial-error results are outside the claim's scope. Training/test-error observations under label noise bear on V1, but the text does not report held-out accuracy on fully random labels or the chance-level comparison.
record.test_reason: The study measures noisy-label memorization and natural generalization in new MNIST settings, bearing on part of V1. Its adversarial-robustness findings do not challenge V1, which concerns natural held-out accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: memorizing label noise can preserve high natural accuracy while substantially harming adversarial robustness. The authors additionally emphasize representation learning and inappropriate invariances as sources of vulnerability.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains networks with partial label noise and reports natural test error, but focuses on adversarial error rather than the full random-label versus natural-label held-out accuracy comparison in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: The toy-MNIST results vary with sample variance and label-noise fraction; full-MNIST experiments vary the label-noise fraction and adversarial perturbation budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitting noisy labels increases adversarial vulnerability even when natural test error remains low.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorizing label noise can impair adversarial robustness without materially impairing natural generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Robust training disproportionately fails on high-self-influence training examples and on visually similar test examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial training can sacrifice natural accuracy by failing to fit rare subpopulations.

record.problems: Natural test-error values relevant to V1 are shown only in figures and are not numerically stated in the text. The reported natural-test results use partial label noise, not fully random labels, and do not provide a chance-level held-out comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Other reported results concern adversarial error, adversarial training, influence/self-influence, decision boundaries, or robust accuracy and do not measure a listed version's specified outcome.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fully randomized labels; chance-level held-out accuracy under fully randomized labels; the complete matched comparison between natural-label and random-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples compared with removing equally many random examples.

missing.what: Low-variance toy-MNIST conditions have high training error because the network cannot memorize label noise, while natural and adversarial test errors remain low. These materially qualify the memorization-capacity result.

A naturally trained CNN attains 100% training accuracy on MNIST with 15% of training labels randomized. This provides explicit numerical evidence of partial-noise fitting, though no corresponding natural test accuracy is stated.

record.verdict_notes: Remove R2's limits_scope verdict: increasing natural error under increasing label noise does not itself contradict V1. The study neither performs V8's removal experiment nor tests V7 through its margin and decision-boundary observations.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report held-out accuracy on fully random labels or compare it with chance; tests partial label noise and natural test error, including a toy MNIST setting and full MNIST.

rows.subject: neural network with four fully connected layers followed by a softmax layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on toy-MNIST data with a fraction of training labels flipped; plotted training and test error as label-noise fraction varied.
rows.measure: Natural test error alongside training error under label noise.
rows.value: figure only; the authors state that test error remains very close to 0 over a range of η values
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval shown; numerical bounds not stated
rows.note: The text says that for σ² = 1, test error remains very close to 0 over a range of label-noise values, while training error reaches zero as the network fits the noisy labels. Exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Valid evidence for coexistence under partial label noise: zero training error and near-zero natural test error at σ² = 1 over a range of noise fractions. It does not establish the fully random-label comparison.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, Figure 3; lines 382–400 describe the architecture, 4000 training samples, interpolation and near-zero natural test error at σ² = 1. Figure 3 caption states 95% confidence intervals.

rows.subject: ReLU network with 4 convolutional layers and two fully connected layers
rows.size_stated: convolutional layers have 32, 64, 128, 256 output filters; fully connected hidden dimension 1024
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with a uniformly random fraction of training labels assigned randomly; natural test accuracy measured as η varied.
rows.measure: Natural test error as label-noise fraction varies.
rows.value: figure only; the authors state that natural test error grows much more slowly than adversarial error
rows.note: The text describes the natural test-error trend but gives no exact values. The plotted adversarial error is outside this version's scope.
rows.check: The supplied text reports natural test error increasing more slowly than adversarial error, but gives neither readable natural-error values nor training error for this experiment. That relative trend alone cannot establish or weaken V1. Figure 4's caption also reports negligible between-run variance, contrary to the row's uncertainty field.
